decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn left gripper toward the purple nut with small continuous elbow-up motion; keep right arm parked.
Finish vertical orientation and approach the purple nut, stopping above grasp depth to check centering.
Correct purple nut centering using calibrated head view, descend, close fully, and lift to verify retention.
Purple nut is visibly retained. Carry it above the matching left screw with vertical clearance, then inspect alignment.
Lower the retained purple nut onto the visually centered screw and start a gentle clockwise turn.
Turn the purple nut clockwise while maintaining alignment and a small downward thread-following motion.
Seat the purple nut a little lower with a small centering correction, then open and reset wrist for another tightening stroke.
Purple nut fell beside the screw rather than seating. Reacquire it at its visible table location with a vertical grasp.
Lift slowly to verify the off-center purple grasp before further transfer or insertion.
Previous lift showed no retention. Open, center over the visible purple nut, and descend to the lower table-grasp height before closing.
Lift the centered purple nut clear of the table and move above its screw; inspect bore alignment before descent.
Use wrist view to remove lateral offset and lower purple nut toward the screw tip; no tightening until engagement is visible.
Screw tip is now visible in the purple bore. Lower gently to engage and apply a clockwise tightening stroke with the gripper closed.
Purple screw tip fills the bore without the earlier table gap. Release only the jaws, reset wrist counterclockwise, and regrasp for continued tightening.
Continue clockwise purple tightening, following the thread downward by a small amount while preserving the upright axis.
Reset the open left wrist without lifting the seated purple nut, then close again for the next clockwise stroke.
Apply another controlled clockwise purple tightening stroke, following the thread downward by 2.5 mm.
Open and reset left wrist while leaving the purple nut seated, then regrasp for additional tightening.
Further clockwise tightening of the seated purple nut, with a small downward thread-following increment.
Reset left wrist for a final purple tightening stroke while raising the right arm within its own workspace for later nut transfer.
Finish another purple clockwise stroke while positioning the open right gripper above its side of the middle transfer area.
Release the tightened purple pair and lift clear; move the left gripper above the yellow nut for a middle-table transfer.
Descend open over the yellow nut, making a small head-view centering correction; check the wrist image before closing.
Center yellow nut between the fingers using the wrist image, close fully, and lift to verify it is retained.
Yellow nut is visibly held. Lift for clearance and carry it to the center handover area; move the right hand aside without crossing arms.
Place the yellow nut upright at the center for a table handover, release, and lift the left fingers clear while the right hand waits.
Withdraw the left arm into its workspace before moving the open right gripper above the centered yellow nut.
Descend the open right gripper onto the yellow nut at the middle handover point, checking centering before grasping.
Make a small wrist-view centering correction, grasp the yellow nut with the right hand, and lift to verify the table handover.
Carry the visibly retained yellow nut above its matching right screw. Independently position the open left hand above the red nut, keeping the arms separated.
Lower the yellow nut toward its screw tip while the open left hand descends over the red nut; inspect both wrist views before grasping or tightening.
Center and seat the yellow nut before a gentle clockwise stroke. Lower the left fingers to the red nut, close fully, then lift to verify retention.
Continue clockwise yellow tightening with the screw tip centered in its bore. Carry the retained red nut above the middle handover point.
Place and release the red nut at the middle for later pickup. Reset the open right wrist around the seated yellow nut and regrasp.
Tighten the seated yellow nut clockwise while withdrawing the open left arm clear of the center and back into its own workspace.
Reset the open right wrist and regrasp the seated yellow nut. Bring the left arm gradually toward its origin with continuous elbow-up posture.
Finish the left arm's gradual return to origin and apply another clockwise yellow tightening stroke after allowing the right grasp to settle.
Keep the left hand open at origin. Reset and regrasp the yellow nut without lifting it for a final controlled tightening stroke.
Apply a final clockwise stroke to the aligned yellow nut, following the thread slightly downward; keep the left hand open at origin.
Release the yellow pair and lift clear. Move the open right gripper above the red nut at the middle handover point, resetting the wrist in transit.
Descend the open right fingers over the centered red nut, correcting the small gripper tilt and checking the wrist view before closing.
Lower the right fingers to the red nut's grasp height, close fully, and lift to verify retention before transfer to its screw.
Red nut is visibly retained. Raise for clearance and carry it above its matching screw in the right workspace; inspect alignment before lowering.
Lower the retained red nut toward its matching screw, correcting the small lateral offset seen in the right wrist view before tightening.
Correct the red nut toward the visible screw tip on the left side of its bore, then lower gently; verify full centering before rotation.
Remove the remaining red bore offset with a small lateral correction, then begin a slow clockwise engagement stroke with gentle descent.
Make a small red centering correction in the updated wrist view, then continue the clockwise stroke with minimal downward travel.
Pause red rotation because a side gap remains. Ease upward slightly, correct toward the screw tip in the wrist image, and reseat slowly.
Red engagement is still uncertain. Lift slowly with the jaws closed to clear contact and check whether the nut remains centered and retained.
Red nut remains retained after lifting. Correct the small sideways offset toward the visible cap, then approach again slowly without rotation.
Screw cap is nearly centered inside the red bore. Finish the small approach and apply a slow clockwise engagement stroke.
Correct the red nut toward the off-center cap without turning, ease it down, then open the fingers to check whether it seats upright on the screw.
Red nut did not remain seated. Move the open right gripper to its new table location and reset the wrist for a centered regrasp.
The close approach encountered interference beside the red screw. Lift clear, turn the jaws perpendicular to the nut–screw separation, and align above the nut for a safer regrasp.
Descend vertically onto the red nut with the jaws oriented away from the adjacent screw, then close for a centered regrasp.
Lift the newly centered red grasp clear of the adjacent screw, then move above the screw axis and inspect before another insertion.
Lower the centered red grasp toward the screw while correcting the cap's slight rightward offset in the wrist view; keep rotation fixed until engagement is visible.
Remove the remaining small red cap offset with millimeter-scale translation and descent, then hold still to check seating before any rotation.
Apply a short slow clockwise red engagement stroke with minimal downward following, keeping the screw axis fixed.
Pause rotation; ease the red nut clear of contact, correct toward the cap on the right of its bore, and reseat slowly with a fixed upright orientation.
The visible side gap has narrowed. Make a final small lateral red alignment adjustment, reseat gently, and hold for a clear engagement check.
The red bore no longer shows a side gap. Open and reset the right wrist without lifting the nut, then regrasp for tightening; keep left at origin.
Red nut is tilted rather than threaded. Lift it free and move to a clear patch in the right workspace to set it upright before a fresh centered grasp.
The red nut did not travel with the lifted hand. Return open above the red pair at a safe viewing height to assess its resting orientation before regrasping.
Red nut is resting tilted against its screw. Approach its visible body with open fingers, keeping clear of the screw and checking the grasp geometry before closing.
Grasp the tilted red nut's body and lift slowly away from the screw to verify retention before attempting to restore its upright orientation.
Previous lift showed no retention. Approach the tilted red nut with open fingers at a lower grasp height, keeping the wrist fixed and watching for screw interference.
Close around the lower part of the tilted red nut and lift vertically in small increments to check retention without dragging the screw.
Move the closed right grasp slowly upward and away from the screw to distinguish retained red nut from contact with the stationary pair.
The red nut stayed on the table. Reposition open over its body, offset from the screw, rather than repeating the previous off-center grasp.
Clear the interference by lifting open, restore the vertical wrist axis, and shift above the red nut's updated resting position for a fresh visual alignment.
The red nut is now separate from the screw but on its side. Approach its body at the calibrated location, grasp gently with closed-position control, and lift to verify retention.
The red nut has settled upright and separate from the screw. Open, center over its bore using the wrist image, descend to table grasp height, and close.
The approach is constrained by the adjacent screw. Open and lift clear, then rotate the jaws away from the screw–nut separation before attempting another centered grasp.
With the jaws now clear of the screw, restore the vertical gripper axis, center over the upright red nut, and descend open for a checked grasp.
Correct the red nut's clearly leftward offset in the current wrist orientation, lowering only slightly with open fingers; check centering before closure.
